messages:
Emma (docs): Quick heads-up, I opened a docs PR to standardize SOC2 wording around retention and add concrete examples for audit logs vs service logs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2498 :mag_right:

Olivia (security): Thanks. Main ask: make the security intent explicit — "retention windows are configurable per-tenant; audit logs have a minimum default of 90 days for SOC2 evidence". Also include guidance on retention enforcement vs soft-delete (we use soft-delete + purge job).

Emma (docs): Added a short note: "Default audit-log retention: 90 days (hosted). Admins can configure up to 7 years via Dedicated/Private." Draft includes a short lifecycle example and a sample purge-schedule YAML.

Ben (infra): For the purge example please call out the implementation caveat: we mark events with `deleted_at` and the purge worker removes blobs after 30 days post-deleted_at. That detail matters for compliance reviewers.

Nora (devex): Can we add a quick SDK snippet showing how to query retention metadata? Customers often want a one-liner to list retention settings for a project. I can add a Python and a curl example.

Emma (docs): Good idea. Draft now includes: curl example and Python snippet (requests) that calls GET /v2/retention/projects/{id}. Also included mapping from old `ttl_days` to new `retention.period` in a tiny migration note.

Alice (legal): Wording nit: avoid phrasing like "we delete data after X". Prefer: "Redwood enforces tenant-configured retention policies; deletion is performed per the configured schedule. Customers with Dedicated/Private deployments can retain or override per contractual terms." Also we need to add a legal-hold exception subsection (how to request, metadata stored as `legal_hold_id`).

Emma (docs): Updated phrasing to match. Added legal-hold subsection with sample JSON for a hold request and the consent/audit entry stored in metadata.

Raj (product): UX suggestion: show a tiny decision flow bullet: hosted = default 90d redaction-first, dedicated = admin console controls retention, private = operator-managed. Keep it compact.

Olivia (security): Also add a short checklist for SOC2 reviewers: retention evidence path (export steps), integrity checks (sha256), and proof of deletion (purge job logs). Maybe link to the audit-export docs.

Emma (docs): I linked to the export doc but the link is stale. Does someone know the new slug? I changed to /docs/audit-exports but CI flagged a broken link.

Ben (infra): New slug is /integrations/audit-exports. I can add a redirect but for now update the doc link.

Emma (docs): Updated link to /integrations/audit-exports. Also added a small code block showing the purge job output for proof-of-deletion: ```
[2025-11-07T08:22:01Z] INFO purge_worker: purged export_2025_10_01, removed 1241 events, checksum: sha256:abcd...
```

Nora (devex): For the SDK example please add header note: `X-Redwood-Retention-Version: 2025-1` — had a couple of customers break on that when migrating.

Emma (docs): Done. Also included a quick mapping table (v1 -> v2) showing `ttl_days` -> `retention.period` and `retain_for_legal_hold` -> `legal_hold_id`.

Alice (legal): One more: add a retention-dispute workflow: how customers request extended retention for investigations and how we log the consent. That needs to be preserved for SOC2 audit.

Emma (docs): Added a short step list: request via console/API -> legal review -> consent recorded (consent_id in metadata) -> retention rule applied.

Raj (product): Looks good. Tiny language nit: use "export package" not "export bundle" for consistency (docs glossary).

CI-bot: docs/pr-2498  linkcheck failed (one broken link fixed) :white_check_mark:

Emma (docs): Thanks! I'll ask Olivia and Alice to do a final pass and then merge tomorrow morning unless anyone objects. :coffee:
